title: FTC OQ-04: Banach-Valued Generalization via Bochner Integral
description: Proves both FTC forms for vector-valued functions F: ℝ → E with E a Banach space using the Bochner integral. Concrete instances for ℝ × ℝ-valued and (Fin n → ℝ)-valued functions. 10 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for Bochner integrals (Lebesgue-Pettis theorem generalization) states: if F: ℝ → E has derivative f and f is Bochner integrable, then ∫_a^b f dt = F(b) - F(a).
overview.problemStatement: Prove both FTC forms for Bochner integrals in Banach spaces, showing the ℝ → ℝ case is a special instance.
overview.proofStrategy: Use Mathlib's IntervalIntegral.FundThmCalculus which is already stated for arbitrary Banach spaces. ftc2_banach: ∫f = F(b) - F(a). ftc1_banach: d/dx ∫_a^x f = f(x). Concrete: ℝ × ℝ and Fin n → ℝ instances.
keyInsights: **Universal Banach statement**: Mathlib's FTC machinery is already parametric in E — the ℝ → ℝ case requires no special treatment.
**Bochner integral**: generalization of Lebesgue integral to Banach-valued functions. Measurability and integrability are stronger requirements than in the scalar case.
**Concrete instances**: ftc2_product (ℝ×ℝ-valued) and ftc2_pi (Fin n → ℝ-valued) demonstrate the generality.

sections.title: FTC for Bochner Integrals in Banach Spaces
sections.summary: ftc2_banach: ∫F' = F(b) - F(a). ftc1_banach: d/dx ∫_a^x f = f(x). ftc2_product, ftc2_pi concrete instances.
sections.mathContext: $\int_a^b F'(t)\,dt = F(b) - F(a)$ for Bochner integrable $F': \mathbb{R} \to E$.

conclusion.summary: 10 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Banach-valued FTC proved via Bochner integral.
conclusion.implications: Banach-valued FTC is essential for differential equations in infinite-dimensional spaces (semigroup theory, PDEs).
openQuestions: Can Gronwall's inequality be proved for Bochner-integrable functions?
Can the Picard-Lindelöf theorem be generalized to Banach-valued ODEs?
Can the Stokes theorem be proved for differential forms valued in Banach spaces?
